title: Variant-aware allocation sweeper for KV fragmentation and GPU footprint tuning (Llama/Mistral/Qwen, long-context)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: For long-context workloads with variant model families (Llama/Mistral/Qwen) we observe intermittent token latency spikes and elevated OOM risk driven by KV cache fragmentation + suboptimal residency patterns during continuous batching. Current allocator heuristics are generic and do not account for model variant shapes (per-layer KV size, attention key density) or long-sequence working sets. This ticket implements a variant-aware 'allocation sweeper' that periodically re-evaluates residency maps, performs targeted compaction (non-blocking when possible), and biases allocator decisions based on observed batch/sequence distributions per model variant and per config (e.g., 32K/64K contexts).
acceptance_criteria: Reduce tail token-latency (p99) for variant long-context workloads by >= 20% under continuous batching compared to baseline runtime-1.20
Decrease transient OOM events for KV-heavy variants by 90% in nightly stress tests with synthetic 50k token sessions
New allocator must expose per-variant telemetry: residency curve, fragmentation ratio, compaction count, compaction time
No regression (<= 3%) in median latency for short-context workloads (<2k tokens), and unit tests for compaction safety
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rolloutable per-customer; documented config knobs in Console
implementation_notes: Design: maintain lightweight per-variant residency maps updated from the runtime's allocation plane; residency map is an approximate histogram (bucketized by layer and kv-slice size) to keep memory bounded
Sweeper runs at configurable cadence (default 60s) and computes fragmentation score = free_gaps_weighted_by_size / total_allocated; threshold triggers compaction pass

Compaction strategy: prefer local (within GPU/allocator arena) slide of KV slices; avoid global GPU-wide copies unless fragmentation exceeds emergency threshold; compaction uses copy-on-write paths to preserve serving reads
Allocator bias: when creating new KV slices, prefer slab buckets sized to model-variant median kv-slice size; this reduces future fragmentation for that variant
Integration with continuous batching: annotate batches with variant ID and sequence-length histogram; sweeper uses this to predict working-set shape and pre-reserve small hot-slab pools
Safety: compaction pauses new allocations for affected arena but keeps in-flight token generation working using old pointers until references switch over
Fallback: when compaction is incompatible with quantized kernels for certain variants, fallback to eviction-based policy and mark variant as 'compaction-incompatible' in telemetry
test_plan: Unit tests: residency map updates, fragmentation score calculation, compaction safety and pointer switchover simulation
Integration: end-to-end on dedicated test cluster running Llama-2-70B, Mistral-22B, Qwen-32B variants with synthetic long sessions (20k/50k tokens) under continuous batching at 5-20 qps
Perf benchmarks: run baseline (runtime-1.20) vs feature gate on (runtime-1.22) comparing p50/p95/p99 token latencies and GPU memory high-water mark
Chaos: induce random allocation churn and device memory pressure; ensure compaction does not increase overall error rate or auth token failures
Canary rollout: enable for internal dedicated customer group, monitor Console metrics for fragmentation_ratio, compactions_per_min, compaction_ms, token_latency_p99
risks: Compaction may increase short-lived CPU/GPU copy overhead under high QPS; need to quantify and gate with adaptive cadence
Incompatibility with some custom quant kernels could force fallback and complicate telemetry interpretation
Incorrect residency heuristics could hurt multi-tenant isolation if slabs reserved for one variant are hoarded by another; require per-tenant tagging
Complexity of pointer switchover could lead to subtle correctness bugs if reference counting is off—requires careful validation
